newsitem.title: TURKEY: Turkish central bank sells dlrs for lira-bankers.
newsitem.headline: Turkish central bank sells dlrs for lira-bankers.

text.p: Turkey's central bank began selling dollars for lira to Turkish banks on Thursday afternoon to restrain the U.S. currency's rise on excess liquidity spilling over from Wednesday, bankers said.
The lira firmed to 107,150 against the dollar on central bank intervention from a previous 107,300.
It had opened at 107,180 after Wednesday's 107,260 close, but weakened later amid a cash surplus.
The central bank had also intervened on Tuesday and Wednesday to curb strong year-end dollar demand which was further buoyed by lower money rates on Wednesday.
Bankers said year-end demand was due to bank's attempts to close their short currency positions as well as importers' foreign currency purchases.

Overnight money rates firmed to 76 percent from an earlier low of 64 percent due to the central bank's dollar sales which drained cash from the market, bankers said. Wednesday's average overnight rate was 57.51 percent.
